overall.summary: The heavy daytime use hypothesis says day minutes raise the chance steadily from the lightest users upwards, but the part adds nothing below about 218 minutes. Three sentences round 4.45% up to 'about 5%'. The rest reproduces.

findings.statement: daytime minutes raise it steadily from the lightest users upwards
findings.check: probe --sweep 'total day minutes=50:300:11' (typical customer, no voice-mail plan); C088 threshold 218 minutes; lint (hinge with no hinge phrase)
findings.evidence: ann_79 contribution 0 (off) from 50 to 200 minutes (risk flat 2.3%), +0.178 at 225, +0.721 at 250, +1.808 at 300 minutes. Nothing below about 218 minutes (C088), so not 'from the lightest users upwards'.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-7a480c --sweep "total day minutes=50:300:11"

findings.statement: ... rises steadily from about 2% to about 5%
findings.evidence: C086 gives 2.26% -> 4.45%, which rounds to about 4%
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify recheck experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-7a480c

findings.statement: from 112 to 249 minutes the chance goes from about 2% to about 5% without one
from about 2% at 112 to about 5% at 249 minutes
full AUC 0.910; all hidden parts mean-ablated 0.717
findings.evidence: 0.9095; four leaves mean-ablated 0.7153 (the always-on relay left in place)
commands: scratch multiablate.py vb-7a480c ann_81 ann_79 ann_80 ann_82 --mean

commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify ablate experiments/verifier_bench/items/vb-7a480c --part ann_81 --to mean
